paper_title: Radiogenomic signatures reveal multiscale intratumour heterogeneity associated with biological functions and survival in breast cancer
prediction_task: Breast cancer survival prediction from MRI radiomics + genomic features

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The model has too many parameters. 24 parameters with 47+40 cases — model is overparametrized. Maximum ~8-10 parameters. They've got (10+10+19)×3=117 parameters — almost infinite ways to extract n from 117 to build models. How did they arrive at these models/parameters?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We performed LASSO regularization with nested cross-validation and reported the number of retained features. Added comparison with simpler models.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Calculated subtraction images without dividing by precontrast image — makes comparison of histogram features (mean, range, min, max) across patients highly dubious. Both in-plane resolution and slice thickness vary — should interpolate to same resolution prior to feature calculations.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We added image normalization and resampling to uniform resolution. Results remain consistent after standardization.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: None of the prognosis analyses correct for common clinical features such as age, size, grade, stage, hormone receptor status. It is important to know if the radiogenomic biomarkers are independent of these clinical features.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We added multivariate Cox regression adjusting for age, stage, grade, and receptor status. Radiogenomic signature remained an independent predictor.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Figure 4d and 7d appear to be training set performance — if so should NOT be reported as it is not representative of unseen data.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We clarified these are cross-validated results, not training performance, and relabeled figures.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Several gene expression signatures for breast cancer (Mammaprint, OncotypeDX) are clinically used. Authors have to study how their proposed biomarkers add additional prognostic value on top of these existing prognostic biomarkers.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We added comparison with established genomic signatures and showed complementary prognostic information.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: IRB/informed consent information not provided. Radiomics methodology needs more detail — software validation, grey level reduction, normalization method.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We added IRB information and detailed radiomics methodology including software (PyRadiomics), grey levels, and normalization steps.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: MRI data quality is no longer state-of-the-art/outdated. Since the TCGA/I-SPY studies there have been significant improvements in MRI software and hardware. Results may not be representative of current MRI radiomics potential.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: We acknowledged the data age limitation and discussed how modern MRI would likely improve results.

reviewer_strengths.text: Solid paper with good design using multiple publicly available datasets. The idea has never been performed in breast cancer and results are very promising. Very well written and logical.
